```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_metafor <- requireNamespace("metafor", quietly = TRUE)
```

This vignette runs end to end without a network connection or a language
model. The three trials below are made up for illustration, and the "model"
is a small function that returns fixed answers. In a real review you pass
your own model callback, and the text comes from `fulltext()` or
`pdftext()`.

The extraction workflow is:

1. `form()` defines what to extract;
2. `extract()` asks the model to fill the form, with a verbatim quote for
   every value;
3. `verify()` checks every value against the source text and basic rules;
4. `agreement()` compares two independent extractions;
5. `studies()` groups records that report the same trial;
6. `effectsizes()` turns effect data into a table ready for `metafor` or
   `meta`.

```{r}
library(medrev)
```

## Records

`medrev()` builds a review from records you already have, such as a
database export. Here the abstracts carry the data.

```{r}
recs <- data.frame(
  pmid = c("100001", "100002", "100003"),
  title = c(
    "Drug X versus placebo in septic shock: the ALPHA randomised trial",
    "Drug X in septic shock: one-year outcomes of the ALPHA trial",
    "Drug X for severe sepsis in primary hospitals: the BETA trial"
  ),
  year = c(2021, 2023, 2022),
  abstract = c(
    paste("ALPHA (NCT01234567) was a multicentre randomised trial in 12 ICUs in France.",
          "We enrolled 400 adults with septic shock between 2018 and 2020; 41% were female.",
          "Patients received drug X (n = 200) or placebo (n = 200).",
          "At 28 days, 50 of 200 patients in the drug X group and 70 of 200 in the placebo group had died",
          "(odds ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.40 to 0.95).",
          "ICU length of stay was 8.1 days (SD 3.2) with drug X and 9.4 days (SD 3.6) with placebo."),
    paste("This report gives one-year outcomes of the ALPHA trial (NCT01234567).",
          "By one year, 82 of 200 patients given drug X and 97 of 200 given placebo had died."),
    paste("BETA was a randomised trial in 6 hospitals in Morocco (NCT07654321).",
          "A total of 240 adults with severe sepsis were assigned to drug X (n = 120) or usual care (n = 120).",
          "Death at 28 days occurred in 30 of 120 and 36 of 120 patients respectively",
          "(odds ratio 0.78, 95% CI 0.44 to 1.38).")
  )
)
r <- medrev(recs, source = "illustration")
r
```

## Chunks

`chunk()` cuts each text into windows that are passed to the model. Here
each abstract is one chunk.

```{r}
ch <- chunk(r, size = 200, which = "all")
ch
```

## Forms

A form lists the fields to extract, with their type. `form("sr")` holds
study characteristics (one row per study); `form("ma")` holds effect data
(one row per outcome, comparison and timepoint).

```{r}
form("sr")
form("ma", measure = "binary")
```

Fields can be added or dropped:

```{r}
sr_form <- form("sr", add = c(dose = "drug X dose and schedule"),
                drop = c("age", "funding", "period"))
```

## A scripted model

Any function that takes a prompt and returns a string works as `llm`. This
one looks up the record id in the prompt and replies with a fixed JSON
answer. One value is wrong on purpose: the BETA sample size is given as 250
while its quote says 240.

```{r}
q <- function(value, quote) list(value = value, quote = quote)

answers_sr <- list(
  "pmid:100001" = list(
    design = q("RCT", "multicentre randomised trial"),
    registration = q("NCT01234567", "ALPHA (NCT01234567)"),
    country = q("France", "12 ICUs in France"),
    setting = q("12 ICUs", "12 ICUs in France"),
    population = q("adults with septic shock", "400 adults with septic shock"),
    n_total = q(400, "We enrolled 400 adults"),
    female_pct = q(41, "41% were female"),
    intervention = q("drug X", "Patients received drug X"),
    comparator = q("placebo", "or placebo"),
    outcomes = q("28-day mortality; ICU length of stay", "At 28 days"),
    follow_up = q("28 days", "At 28 days")),
  "pmid:100002" = list(
    design = q("RCT", "outcomes of the ALPHA trial"),
    registration = q("NCT01234567", "ALPHA trial (NCT01234567)"),
    follow_up = q("1 year", "By one year")),
  "pmid:100003" = list(
    design = q("RCT", "BETA was a randomised trial"),
    registration = q("NCT07654321", "Morocco (NCT07654321)"),
    country = q("Morocco", "6 hospitals in Morocco"),
    n_total = q(250, "A total of 240 adults"),
    intervention = q("drug X", "assigned to drug X"),
    comparator = q("usual care", "or usual care"),
    follow_up = q("28 days", "Death at 28 days"))
)

answers_ma <- list(
  "pmid:100001" = list(
    list(outcome = q("mortality", "had died"), timepoint = q("28 days", "At 28 days"),
         n_e = q(200, "50 of 200"), n_c = q(200, "70 of 200"),
         events_e = q(50, "50 of 200"), events_c = q(70, "70 of 200"),
         measure = q("OR", "odds ratio 0.62"), estimate = q(0.62, "odds ratio 0.62"),
         ci_low = q(0.40, "95% CI 0.40 to 0.95"), ci_high = q(0.95, "95% CI 0.40 to 0.95"))),
  "pmid:100002" = list(
    list(outcome = q("mortality", "had died"), timepoint = q("1 year", "By one year"),
         n_e = q(200, "82 of 200"), n_c = q(200, "97 of 200"),
         events_e = q(82, "82 of 200"), events_c = q(97, "97 of 200"))),
  "pmid:100003" = list(
    list(outcome = q("mortality", "Death at 28 days"), timepoint = q("28 days", "Death at 28 days"),
         n_e = q(120, "drug X (n = 120)"), n_c = q(120, "usual care (n = 120)"),
         events_e = q(30, "30 of 120"), events_c = q(36, "36 of 120"),
         measure = q("OR", "odds ratio 0.78"), estimate = q(0.78, "odds ratio 0.78"),
         ci_low = q(0.44, "95% CI 0.44 to 1.38"), ci_high = q(1.38, "95% CI 0.44 to 1.38")))
)

scripted_model <- function(answers, rows) {
  function(prompt, ...) {
    id <- names(answers)[vapply(names(answers), grepl, logical(1), x = prompt, fixed = TRUE)][1]
    ans <- answers[[id]]
    jsonlite::toJSON(if (rows) list(rows = ans) else ans, auto_unbox = TRUE)
  }
}
```

## Extraction for a systematic review

```{r}
sr <- extract(ch, scripted_model(answers_sr, rows = FALSE), form = sr_form,
              model = "scripted")
extractions(sr)[, c("record_id", "design", "registration", "country", "n_total", "follow_up")]
```

With `quotes = TRUE` every value comes with the text that supports it:

```{r}
extractions(sr, quotes = TRUE)[3, c("n_total", "n_total_quote")]
```

## Checking the values

`verify()` runs deterministic checks. Quotes are looked up in the chunks
the model saw, numbers are looked up in their quote, and effect data are
checked for impossible values (events above the arm size, an estimate
outside its interval, and so on).

```{r}
issues <- verify(sr, ch)
issues[issues$severity != "note", c("record_id", "field", "check", "message")]
```

The wrong sample size is flagged, and so is the fact that two records share
one trial registration.

## Two reviewers

Systematic reviews extract in duplicate. Run a second extraction (another
model, another prompt, or a human's table loaded with the same form) and
compare:

```{r}
answers_sr2 <- answers_sr
answers_sr2[["pmid:100003"]]$n_total <- q(240, "A total of 240 adults")
sr2 <- extract(ch, scripted_model(answers_sr2, rows = FALSE), form = sr_form,
               model = "second")
ag <- agreement(sr, sr2)
ag[ag$status != "agree", c("record_id", "field", "value_a", "value_b", "status")]
```

## Records and studies

The first two records report the same trial. `studies()` groups records by
their registration number:

```{r}
st <- studies(sr)
st
```

## Extraction for a meta-analysis

The `"ma"` form returns as many rows per record as the paper reports.

```{r}
ma <- extract(ch, scripted_model(answers_ma, rows = TRUE),
              form = form("ma", measure = "binary"), model = "scripted")
verify(ma, ch)
```

`effectsizes()` computes one effect size per row, on the log scale for ratio
measures. It uses the reported estimate and CI when available and falls back
to the 2x2 counts otherwise; `derived` and `note` record which.

```{r}
es <- effectsizes(ma, study = st)
es[, c("study", "timepoint", "measure", "estimate", "yi", "sei", "derived")]
```

## Pooling

The table plugs into `metafor` (or `meta::metagen(TE = yi, seTE = sei)`).
Pool the 28-day mortality rows, one per study:

```{r, eval = has_metafor}
d28 <- as.data.frame(es[es$timepoint == "28 days", ])
fit <- metafor::rma(yi, vi, data = d28, method = "REML", slab = study)
fit
metafor::forest(fit, atransf = exp, xlab = "Odds ratio (28-day mortality)")
```

## Using a real model

Replace the scripted model with any function that calls your model. For
example with `ellmer`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
chat <- ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-4.1")
my_model <- function(prompt, ...) chat$clone()$chat(prompt, echo = "none")

ft <- pdftext(r, dir = "pdfs")          # or fulltext(r) for PMC open access
ch <- chunk(r, fulltext = ft)
sr <- extract(ch, my_model, form = form("sr"))
ma <- extract(ch, my_model, form = form("ma"))
verify(ma, ch)
```
